original_question: Characterize all multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} that admit a C_k-representation: there exist functions phi, Phi in L-P+ and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s), where B_m^phi(u)=sum_{r=0}^m binom(m,r)(1-u)^r a_{m-r} u^{m-r} when phi(x)=sum_{m>=0} a_m x^m/m!.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 8: "Characterize all multiplier sequences which have a C_k-representation," read together with Section 4, Definition 6 and Eq. (4.2)/(4.3), and the partial positive results in Theorem 19. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target: it correctly identifies that the problem is to characterize multiplier sequences admitting a C_k-representation, it uses the right Section 4 parametrization gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s), it keeps phi and Phi in L-P^+, and it gives the coefficient formula for B_m^phi(u) compatible with the paper’s generating-function definition. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: You should say explicitly that "multiplier sequence" means a classical multiplier sequence over R, i.e. the diagonal operator T[x^k] = gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness of real polynomials. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

You should specify the ambient function class: phi and Phi are entire functions in the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative Taylor coefficients, denoted L-P^+. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

Definition 6 allows phi and Phi to be not necessarily distinct; that should be stated to match the paper exactly. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The quantifier is for all k in N_0. Your draft says k >= 0 globally, but the stand-alone question should attach that quantifier directly to the representation condition. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

The paper’s preferred definition of B_m^phi(u) is via the generating relation e^{(1-u)x} phi(ux) = sum_{m>=0} B_m^phi(u) x^m/m!; the coefficient formula is a consequence and is fine to include, but the generating form is the paper-faithful notation nearby. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

Corollary 18 proves that C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s) is automatically a multiplier sequence for (t,s) in [0,1] x [0,1], whereas Definition 6 itself allows arbitrary real s,t. So the open problem is not to characterize all such parameter choices, but to characterize those classical multiplier sequences that admit some such representation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

Theorem 19 gives two paper-specific families already known to have C_k-representations: polynomially interpolated multiplier sequences of nonnegative terms, and geometric multiplier sequences. Including this nearby scope keeps the question aligned with the paper’s exact intent and prevents accidental broadening. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Characterize precisely the classical multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} of real numbers for which there exist entire functions phi, Phi in L-P^+ (not necessarily distinct) and real parameters t,s such that, for every k in N_0, gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s) := sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s), where B_m^phi(u) is defined by e^{(1-u)x} phi(ux) = sum_{m>=0} B_m^phi(u) x^m/m! (equivalently, if phi(x) = sum_{m>=0} a_m x^m/m!, then B_m^phi(u) = sum_{r=0}^m binom(m,r)(1-u)^r a_{m-r} u^{m-r}). Here "classical multiplier sequence" means that the operator T on R[x] given by T[x^k] = gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, characterize precisely the classical multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} whose exponential generating function factors in the form sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k! = e^{((1-t)+(1-s))x} phi(tx) Phi(sx) for some phi, Phi in L-P^+ and some real s,t. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
justification: The nearest official formulation is not a conjecture from the introduction but the final open problem of the paper: Problem 8 in Section 5. Definition 6 supplies the exact meaning of "has a C_k-representation," Eq. (4.2) and Eq. (4.3) give the coefficient and generating-function forms of that representation, Corollary 18 explains the [0,1] x [0,1] case in which the construction yields multiplier sequences, and Theorem 19 records the two classes already known to be representable. Your draft captures the core mathematical content well, but it omits the paper’s explicit meaning of multiplier sequence, the not-necessarily-distinct clause for phi and Phi, the paper’s preferred generating-function definition of B_m^phi, and the nearby Section 4 scope that keeps the question faithful rather than broader than intended. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
